scope: Public technique descriptions, detector rules and synthetic agent benchmarks; no third-party raw content redistributed

sources.title: MITRE ATT&CK — Credentials In Files
sources.support: Accessing credential-bearing files can indicate credential access; a read alone does not prove misuse.

sources.title: MITRE ATT&CK — Exfiltration Over Web Service
sources.support: External web services can serve as exfiltration channels; successful transfer requires independent evidence.

sources.title: MITRE ATT&CK — Data Destruction
sources.support: Destructive deletion and overwrite patterns; single unlink need not imply destruction.

sources.title: MITRE ATT&CK — Data Encrypted for Impact
sources.support: Mass file encryption for impact; encryption alone may be authorized.

sources.title: MITRE ATT&CK — Account Manipulation
sources.support: Account privileges or credential changes can establish persistence or privilege escalation.

sources.title: MITRE ATT&CK — Indicator Removal: File Deletion
sources.support: Removal of intrusion artifacts can indicate evasion; ordinary cleanup is common.

sources.title: Falco — Default Rules
sources.support: Sensitive reads, unexpected child shells and suspicious container access are behavioral detections with documented noise/allowlist context.

sources.title: AgentDojo — Dynamic Prompt Injection Benchmark
sources.support: Untrusted tool-result content can redirect tool-using agents away from legitimate user tasks.

sources.title: AgentDojo — Workspace Injection Tasks
sources.support: Defines attacker-targeted tool actions such as email transmission; tasks are simulated benchmark scenarios, not observed Linux syscalls.

sources.title: PrivacyAlign — Human Annotated Synthetic Privacy Benchmark
sources.support: Synthetic agent tool and memory scenarios with human contextual privacy preferences; benchmark labels must not be equated to real exfiltration.

sources.title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026
sources.support: Agent authority, tool misuse and delegated decisions require evidence of approval and execution; OS traces cannot prove prompt injection alone.
